chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad al-Saffar) he said:

A group of people from Khurasan came to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) and asked him to release them from the khums. He said, 'How hasty you are! You claim affection for us with your tongues, but you withhold from us the right that Allah has made for us and we for it, and that is the khums. We will not release any one of you from it.'

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا: Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (Imam Ali al-Rida, AS)

ai.seo_question: What is the Imam's response to those who claim love for the Ahl al-Bayt but seek exemption from khums?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Imam’s discernment between superficial verbal affection and genuine financial commitment, using the payment of khums as a litmus test for true loyalty. Imam al-Rida (AS) asserts that khums is a divine right designated for the Imams, and withholding it while claiming love is a contradiction that precludes exemption. This underscores the Shia theological view that khums is not merely a tax but a spiritual bond linking the community to the Imam’s authority.
